findings: DOMStorage access requires a live frame at the requested origin; an about:blank page cannot read or restore an arbitrary origin, including after a prior visit.

Setting a matching cookie with expires:0 through Storage.setCookies removed it while preserving an unrelated cookie in this one unpartitioned HTTP case. This is a candidate for selective removal, not proven coverage of secure/partitioned/domain/path combinations.

The pinned reference saves local storage from current pages where possible and uses a private page with intercepted blank HTML for other visited origins and restoration. The implementation must preserve closed-page origins, context isolation and avoid application/backend requests during state work.

Implement context-owned temporary storage pages and intercepted origin navigation with cancellation/closure cleanup; do not use upstream browser operations in production.
Add differential HTTP authentication/state fixtures, state file round trips, context isolation, closed-origin collection and network-side-effect checks before claiming the M2 slice.
